ruleName: Ball moved when grounding the club
imagePrompt: A teenage golfer on the fairway unintentionally makes the golf ball move while grounding their club behind it.
imageAlt: Teen golfer causes ball to roll by grounding club behind it on fairway.

issues: Golfer's stance and hand placement are not clearly left-handed; it appears more like a right-handed address
Club face orientation does not clearly indicate a left-handed golfer
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the golfer's posture and hand placement so that it is unmistakably a left-handed stance, with the left hand lower on the grip and the club face oriented as appropriate for a left-handed golfer. Ensure all other details remain unchanged.

questions.title: What happens if you move your ball with your club?
questions.question: You put your club down behind your ball on the fairway and the ball rolls away by accident. What should you do?

choices.text: No penalty. Hit your ball from its new place.
Put your ball back where it was and add 1 penalty shot.
Add two penalty shots and keep playing.
Put your ball back and no penalty.

questions.explanation: If you make your ball move by putting your club on the ground behind it, you must put your ball back and add one penalty shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass you aim for between the tee and the green.
Letting your club touch the ground before you swing.

questions.teachingTip: Show the children how to carefully put their club behind the ball without moving it. Practise where to rest the club gently.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they can hit the ball from where it moved to.
Some may forget to add the penalty stroke.

questions.title: Penalty for moving the ball when grounding the club
questions.question: You accidentally move your ball on the fairway by grounding your club behind it. What must you do according to the rules?

choices.text: No penalty, play the ball from where it moved to.
Replace the ball and add 1 penalty stroke.
Add two penalty strokes and carry on.
Replace the ball with no penalty.

questions.explanation: If you move your ball by grounding your club behind it on the fairway, the correct action is to replace the ball and add one penalty stroke.
